Neurology · published research

Kleine-Levin syndrome

One case report described remission of Kleine-Levin syndrome symptoms during a treatment period using intranasal red-light PBM together with methylene blue. There is no controlled comparison.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One case report described remission of Kleine-Levin syndrome symptoms during a treatment period using intranasal red-light PBM together with methylene blue. There is no controlled comparison.

Summary of the Evidence

The Kleine-Levin syndrome category contains one unique publication, a human case report. It does not include a randomized trial, comparison study, animal model, laboratory experiment or review. The patient was previously described as having persistent symptoms despite other treatments. The report is an observation in one person, not an estimate of average treatment effect.

Human and clinical evidence

Hamper et al. reported one patient with Kleine-Levin syndrome who received intranasal PBM alongside methylene blue. The authors described symptom remission beginning within about a week and continuing during the reported follow-up, which extended over roughly two years (Hamper et al. 2021). Because both treatments were started together and there was no control condition, the report cannot determine whether the change was caused by PBM, methylene blue, their combination or the natural fluctuation of the condition.

Animal evidence

No animal study directly addressing Kleine-Levin syndrome was identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The case report describes intranasal red light at 633 nm together with methylene blue. The database does not provide a complete dose or exposure schedule that could be reproduced from the record alone. An intranasal application also differs from transcranial scalp treatment, and the added drug prevents attribution of the case outcome to light alone.

Interpretation

This case suggests that the combined intervention was followed by a prolonged period without reported symptoms in one patient. It does not establish a treatment effect, show that PBM alone is active or tell whether another person with the syndrome would respond. The absence of a control group and the two-part treatment are the central uncertainties.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for Kleine-Levin syndrome because the evidence is one uncontrolled case using PBM together with methylene blue. No evidence for an independent PBM effect or for other patients.
Publications and records1 unique title

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The only report describes one patient and combines intranasal PBM with methylene blue, so the contribution of either treatment cannot be separated. A larger prospective study with a comparison group, defined relapse outcomes and standardized follow-up would be needed to judge whether the approach changes the course of Kleine-Levin syndrome.
